Full: Flynn, J. R., & Rossi-Casé, L. (2012). IQ gains in Argentina betwen 1964 and 1988.   Intelligence, 40, 145-150.
DB: 1998 group reduced from six to three age-groups (normtable available only untill age 15.5)
L&V: Flynn & Rossi-Casé (2012) give SPM data for 13-14 year olds (assumed to lie between 13.0 and 14.11 years and therefore with a mean of 14.0 years) for the city of  La Plata tested in 1964 and in 1998. The 1964 sample obtained a score of 38 equivalent to the 14th percentile (IQ =84) on the 1979 British standardization, needing a 3 IQ point Flynn effect (15 years) addition to raise it to 87.  They also give SPM data for 17-24 year olds for the city of  La Plata tested in 1964 and in 1998. The 1964 sample obtained a score of 38.9 equivalent to the 5th percentile (IQ =75.3) on the 1992 British standardization, needing a 5.6 IQ point Flynn effect (28 years) addition to raise it to 81.  The two IQs for 1964 have been averaged to 84. The 1998 sample of 13/14 year olds obtained a score of 47.7 equivalent to the 60th percentile (IQ =104) on the 1979 British standardization, needing a 4 IQ point Flynn effect (21 years) reduction to 100.  The 1998 sample 17-24 year olds obtained a score of 50 equivalent to the 28th percentile (IQ =91) on the 1992 British standardization, needing a 1 IQ point Flynn effect (6 years) reduction to 90. The two IQs for 1998 have been averaged to 95. There has therefore been an increase of 11 IQ points in the IQ in Argentina from 1964 to 1992, according to these results, representing 2.5 IQ points a decade.
